questions.question: A physician calls you about a patient with chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS). He has read articles about xenotropic murine leukemia virus-related virus (XMRV) and its link to CFS. He wants to start the patient on treatment and asks for your advice about workup and treatment of XMRV.
questions.question_raw: Physician calls you about a patient with chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS). He has read articles about Xenotropic murine leukemia virus-related virus (XMRV) and its link to CFS. He wants to start the patient on treatment and asks for your advice about workup and treatment of XMRV.

parts.text: What would you advise the physician?

parts_raw.text: What would you advise the physician?

questions.model_answer: a) Advise against any XMRV testing or treatment. The reported association between XMRV and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome has been refuted: the original 2009 Science report and related studies were retracted, the positive results were shown to be laboratory contamination with mouse DNA/XMRV-containing cell-line sequences, and XMRV is a laboratory-derived recombinant virus with no evidence of human infection or disease causation. Multiple blinded multicentre studies (including the NHLBI Blood XMRV Scientific Research Working Group and the Lipkin multicentre study) found no XMRV or polytropic MLV sequences in ME/CFS patients versus controls. There is therefore no validated or clinically indicated assay for XMRV, and no role for antiretroviral therapy (which carries real toxicity without any proven benefit). Instead, evaluate for treatable alternative causes of chronic fatigue (thyroid disease, anemia, sleep apnea, depression, medication effects, occult infection/malignancy), confirm the ME/CFS diagnosis by accepted criteria, and manage supportively: treat comorbid sleep disturbance, pain, orthostatic intolerance and mood disorder, with activity pacing and avoidance of post-exertional symptom exacerbation.
questions.beyond_mandell: Rests on the 2011-2012 retraction of Lombardi et al. (Science) and the Lipkin multicentre blinded study plus IOM/NAM 2015 ME/CFS diagnostic criteria.

cohort_answer.text: There is no association between the virus and CFS.
